source: High Country Fly Fishing Guides and Locals

conditions.overall: Wild water levels are low and larger streams have seen heavy pressure this summer, with some larger rivers on the cusp of being too warm on certain days. More success is being found on smaller, cooler streams at higher elevation.

tactics: Focus on smaller, cooler streams at higher elevation that are off the beaten path — larger wild streams have seen heavy summer pressure and can be too warm some days.
Light and small dry droppers has been the name of the game on wild water.

On the Watauga River, the morning pulse (6–7 AM release) makes the fishing better — that burst of cold water cools everything down and gets the bugs moving. On days without a morning release, fishing has been tougher.
On the South Holston, wade fishermen have opportunities in the morning before the afternoon release; drift boat anglers have water in the afternoon.
Watch for sulphur hatches on the South Holston in the afternoon once the water comes on.
Always check current dam release schedules from TVA before heading out — flows can change without notice.

For delayed harvest streams, use the NC daily stocking report tool to confirm when a stream was stocked before making the trip, as stocking dates are more spread out this year across October and November.

waters.name: Wild Creeks (Western North Carolina)
waters.note: Smaller, cooler wild creeks off the beaten path are producing the most success. Larger wild streams have seen heavy pressure and can be too warm some days.

waters.name: Watauga River (East Tennessee)
waters.note: Morning pulse release (6–7 AM) improves fishing by cooling the water and getting bugs moving. Fishing is tougher on days without a morning release. Expected to improve as temperatures drop closer to October.

waters.name: South Holston (East Tennessee)
waters.note: Releasing water in the afternoon daily. Wade fishermen have morning opportunities; drift boats fish in the afternoon. Sulphur hatches reported in the afternoon when water comes on.

elevation_note: High Country streams (Boone, 3300-4000ft) run 1-2 weeks behind lower-elevation WNC
stocking_note: Delayed harvest stocking begins in approximately two weeks. This year stockings are more spread out across October and November rather than concentrated at the start of the month. Stocking schedule: Helton Creek (Sept 28–Oct 2), Big Horse Creek (Oct 5–9), Watauga River/Valle Crucis & Lower DH (Oct 12–16), New River/Todd Island Park (Oct 12–16), Wilson Creek (Oct 12–16). Use the NC daily stocking report tool to confirm before fishing.
